title: A `for` header's init and increment clauses are refused, not classified, when stripping their grouping tokens is not faithful
why: `split_for_clauses` strips `(`, `)`, `[` and `]` from a `for` header's init and increment clauses (`W4-EXPR-POS-FOR-CLAUSES`, recorded in docs/reports/remaining-w4-expr-pos/README.md and never registered here), so `q_free(p)` in either clause read as the names `q_free p` and lowered to `NoOp`. Card W45-PARENTHESISED-CALLEE (gateway constraint 10c, rule 3) refuses such a clause unless its stripped classification was already a refusal, and keeps the stripped classification only where every group wraps one name (`TAILQ_FOREACH_SAFE`'s `(elm) = (tmpelm)`). On the pinned corpus that refuses 5 clauses in 5 functions already Unknown: 4 `RD_MAP_FOREACH_ELEM` headers whose `rd_map_iter_begin`/`rd_map_iter_next` calls were dropped, and 1 `TAILQ_FOREACH` increment `(e) = ((e)->link.tqe_next)` whose stripped spelling was faithful but whose group wraps a member chain (one `unresolved resource identity` report exchanged). DISCHARGE: classify the two clauses from their original spelling through the ordinary statement classifier, as the condition already is, retire rule 3, and re-pin the corpus with every moved leaf attributed.

title: A call through a callee expression that is not a name is refused
why: Card W45-PARENTHESISED-CALLEE normalises only `(NAME)(...)` (any depth of parentheses) and refuses every other callee expression: a conditional `(c ? f : g)(x)`, an address `(&f)(x)`, a cast `((T) f)(x)`, a comma `(a, f)(x)`, a call's result `g()(x)` and a subscript `a[i](x)`. None of these replaced an admission in the pinned corpus (0 leaves carry the refusal), so the residual is unsized there. DISCHARGE: model the forms C gives a single designator (`(&f)(x)` is `f(x)`; a cast to a function-pointer type of a function designator calls that function) and desugar a conditional callee into its two branches through the W44-BRANCH-CONDITION-CALLS edges, each with Lean parity and a measured re-pin.

title: The gateway tells a cast from a parenthesised callee lexically
why: `(T)(x)` is a cast when `T` is a type and a call when `T` designates a function or object; the gateway has no symbol table at this point and decides from a file-scope typedef declarator reader (`typedef_declarators`) and a per-function object-use over-approximation (`object_use`), both lexical (trust boundary 28). A typedef the reader does not recognise reads its casts as calls, the refusing direction; the unsound direction would be reading a function name as a trusted type, which the reader avoids by counting only declarator positions of file-scope `typedef` declarations and dropping any name the function may use as an object. DISCHARGE: decide the cast/call distinction from the typed Clang AST's `CallExpr`/`CStyleCastExpr` nodes, cross-checked against the lexical reading on the corpus with every disagreement reported, or prove the lexical reader's answer sound for the grammar it reads.
